items.grounds: Re-derived both ways. The finding quotes the row's warrant sentence accurately, and the continuity facts are byte-true: גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier) and אֲבִיתֶֽם (oshb:Isa.30.15, byte tier), with תָּנֻ֑סוּ (oshb:Isa.30.17, byte tier) and נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם (oshb:Isa.30.17, byte tier), carry the second-person plural that the suffix inside the row's own opener וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier) answers. That is cross-seam cohesion straddling the row's own front seam: under the cross-seam law it argues continuity against the cut, so disclosing it is right and naming it 'the seam's real warrant' is a defective warrant. The opening verse's bytes carry a backward-linking consequence connector as first token -- no hoy, no massa, no koh-amar frame, no imperative or vocative onset (first-token and bigram checks, skeleton tier) -- and the row itself states the addressee does not shift. The tier-3 layer re-derives exactly as the finding states: chapter-30 segs are SAMEKH at MT 30:5, 30:11, 30:18, 30:26, 30:33 with PE at MT 30:14, none at MT 30:17, so the nearest marked division falls after the row's opening verse, interior to the span. With only the consequence-connector signal registered, no frame-onset deviation, and frontier_flag_considered false, the warrant defect is real but not alone load-bearing -- the verdict-to-promise turn and the rear seam stand: medium as filed.

Re-swept from bytes. The contiguous consonantal-skeleton substring returns exactly 25 MT verses (staged sweep, verse unit); the word-bound token split of that same hit set is clean: the bare token לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.30.12, byte tier) stands in 23 verses, the waw-prefixed form in exactly 2 -- MT 8:7 and MT 30:18 -- no verse carries both forms, and no third token shape exists in the hit set. The row's 25 digit therefore belongs to the blended substring class while its prose names 'the bare particle', which stands at 23; and the row's own onset is waw-prefixed -- both connector tokens of MT 30:18 are: וְלָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier) and וְלָכֵ֥ן (oshb:Isa.30.18, byte tier) -- while the comparator at MT 30:12 the prose calls 'the same connector' is bare, a form difference never disclosed. A digit attached to the wrong named object beside a warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

Re-swept on first-token identity. Verse-initial matching gives 18 MT verses at consonantal-skeleton tier and 17 at accent-stripped tier; the sole delta member is MT 54:16, a K/Q verse (single-witness inventory, 1 note) whose verse-initial token is the unpointed ketiv הן (oshb:Isa.54.16, byte tier) standing before the pointed qere הִנֵּ֤ה (oshb:Isa.54.16, byte tier) -- at the pointed layer that verse opens with the hinneh presentative, not the hen form at all. The row's own splice הֵ֥ן (oshb:Isa.32.1, byte tier) is the pointed presentative and its digit names no tier, so 18 is mis-owned exactly as claimed: it holds only at skeleton tier and only by counting a ketiv skeleton, the class the K/Q-before-counting rule guards; the pointed form stands verse-initial at 17. The dependent sub-claim survives at both tiers -- the only chapters-28-35 members are MT 32:1 and MT 33:7. An untiered, K/Q-contaminated digit, not alone load-bearing (the row rests the site's discrimination on topic, not on the count): medium as filed.

Mark facts re-derived from the inventory: PE at MT 32:8 -- correctly typed, correctly not conflated with the SAMEKH segs at MT 31:9 and MT 32:20 -- and disclosed single-witness by the row. The defect is weight: device_notes reads 'resting the boundary on the fresh subject (the coming king), the verse-initial presentative, and the parashah PE mark at oshb:Isa.32.8', listing a Prophets parashah mark among the grounds the boundary rests on; under the owner addendum that layer is tier-3 weak corroboration, never a boundary driver, and the row's own boundary_rationale holds the same mark to 'corroborating the break'. The two fields assign the same mark different weights and the device_notes phrasing is the defective one. Not alone load-bearing -- the topic onset and the presentative carry the seam: medium as filed.

Every byte ground re-derives. The summons שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, byte tier) is a verse-initial imperative with named addressees; that verse-initial imperative stands at exactly 10 MT verses book-wide, identical at skeleton and accent-stripped tiers (MT 1:2, 1:10, 33:13, 46:3, 46:12, 48:1, 49:1, 51:1, 51:7, 66:5), MT 33:13 the single chapters-28-35 site. The seg layer carries SAMEKH at MT 33:1, 33:6, 33:12. Under the convention this corpus itself applies -- the row reads the MT 32:20 seg as closing the preceding verse -- the MT 33:12 division falls immediately before the summons, so the row's claim that its interior segs mark turns binding 'to no fresh hoy or vocative marker of their own' is byte-false at exactly the declined site; it is true only at MT 33:6, whose next verse opens on the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, byte tier). The stated decline rule -- absence of a fresh hoy, massa, or divine-frame marker -- also fails to discriminate MT 33:13 from קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, byte tier): first-token and koh-amar-bigram checks at skeleton tier find no hoy, massa, or koh-amar frame in either onset, the row itself calls the two the same formal class, and the neighbouring row cuts at MT 34:1; on the row's stated rule its own rear seam at MT 33:24, which carries no seg, is left without positive warrant. A whole-chapter span held by a decline that omits the tier-1 imperative-onset and addressee-shift class and rests on a byte-false mark-binding claim is a load-bearing defect: high as filed. Span ruling: endorse_proposal -- the respan case is byte-sound (a tier-1 summons onset at MT 33:13, the same signal class the sibling cuts at MT 32:9 and MT 34:1 rest on, with the MT 33:12 SAMEKH as tier-3 corroboration), and the proposal's alternative branch, holding the span under a re-argued decline that does distinguish MT 34:1's scene turn from the continuing Zion scene at MT 33:13-14, stays open to the owner docket; nothing adopted here.

Inventory re-derived exactly as filed: chapter-33 segs are SAMEKH at MT 33:1, 33:6, 33:12 and nothing else inside MT 33:1-33:24; MT 33:24 carries no seg; one paseq at MT 33:14, held count-only by the row, correctly; zero K/Q notes in the chapter; SAMEKH at MT 32:20 ahead of the onset. The row reads the layer both ways at one seam: it takes the MT 32:20 seg as closing the preceding verse immediately ahead of the onset -- the convention its siblings apply at MT 31:9, MT 32:8, and MT 35:10 -- yet writes 'This same onset, oshb:Isa.33.1, is itself marked by a parashah SAMEKH mark' and counts only 'Two further SAMEKH marks ... interior to the unit' at MT 33:6 and MT 33:12. Under the corpus convention the MT 33:1 seg divides MT 33:1 from MT 33:2, interior to the span; it cannot corroborate the onset seam, which the MT 32:20 seg already serves, and the interior tally omits it. A misassigned mark function with the span-relevant disclosure sweep otherwise complete, the hoy onset carrying the seam regardless: medium as filed.

Re-derived. The rear-bound formula is real in the bytes: כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte tier), one of the koh-amar census's exactly 4 royal-messenger verses (MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3) against its 44 divine-frame verses, so the adopted seam is materially right. The shipped row carries that ground only as English prose -- 'opens the Rabshakeh's own royal-messenger speech with a fresh frame formula' -- with web:Isa.36.4 cited, no pointed splice, no tier label, and no oshb:Isa.36.4 in boundary_evidence_refs (the refs hold web:Isa.36.1, web:Isa.36.3, web:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.36.1, and oshb:Isa.35.10, whose PE re-verifies in the inventory). The engagement-class law makes pointed splices plus tier labels mandatory for every boundary-relevant original-language claim; this formula is the rear seam's only original-language ground, and the sibling row covering MT 36:4 splices the same formula at byte tier. An unengaged warrant at the row's own seam -- true in substance, defective in evidentiary carriage, span unaffected: medium as filed.

Re-derived. The onset verse's own bytes open a verse-initial speech frame with full speaker-addressee inversion: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.11, byte tier; the title is two tokens in the staged extract), the three officials now speaking and the Rabshakeh now addressed, the inverse of the frame at oshb:Isa.36.4. The row instead writes 'This short unit turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame', quotes MT 36:11 in English only, splices Hebrew only at oshb:Isa.36.12, and lists no oshb:Isa.36.11 among its refs -- the stated warrant disclaims the tier-1 signal standing in its own onset bytes while the adopted bound is materially right. The finding's collaterals re-sweep clean: the bare hiriq-pointed adonai token stands word-bound at exactly 3 verses, MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12; the two adonai-family forms at MT 36:12, אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte tier) and אֲדֹנִ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte tier), are distinct at byte tier and at finals-normalized skeleton tier; and MT 36:12 is a doubled K/Q verse of the single-witness inventory (2 notes), disclosed by the row. A front-seam warrant defect with the span right: medium as filed.
